text.aria-label: Title text 'Figure 13: Do any inputs help the XGBoost model say how uncertain it is?'

g.text: Figure 13: Do any inputs help the XGBoost model say how uncertain it is?

text.aria-label: Subtitle text 'Six NGED solar farms, daylight hours, September 2019 to June 2026. ERA5: ECMWF's reanalysis of past weather. CAMS: satellite irradiance service. Dot: estimate. Line: 95% interval from resampling whole months. Dashed rule: no difference. Main XGBoost tuning setting only. Each row is the score with the first variable set minus the score with the second. The XGBoost model predicts a 10 to 90% interval that should hold 80% of outcomes. A more accurate forecast also narrows it, so compare with the control. Coverage: the share of outcomes inside the interval. Neither sign is better; the target is 80%. CRPS scores the whole predicted distribution. A variable set is the list of inputs the XGBoost model is given. G0: sun position, ERA5 solar radiation (ssrd), and air temperature (t2m). Each group adds to the one before. G1: total cloud cover. G2: low, mid, and high cloud cover. G3: clear-sky radiation. G4: cloud water and cloud base height. G5: direct beam. G6: wind and thermal radiation. G7: humidity and haze. G8: snow and albedo. G9 (the full set): all other ERA5 variables. G10: G9 plus CAMS aerosol. Negative control: G2 plus shuffled copies of the other variables, which carry no information. MARS-only: 12 ERA5 variables that neither ECMWF's free forecast feed nor Open-Meteo serves. Clearness index: irradiance divided by the irradiance at the top of the atmosphere. Exploratory: not named in the study plan before any result existed, and not corrected for multiple comparisons.'
text.tspan: Six NGED solar farms, daylight hours, September 2019 to June 2026. ERA5: ECMWF's reanalysis of past weather. CAMS:
Dot: estimate. Line: 95% interval from resampling whole months.
Dashed rule: no difference. Main XGBoost tuning setting only. Each row is the score
with the first variable set minus the score with the second.
The XGBoost model predicts a 10 to 90% interval that should hold 80% of outcomes. A
more accurate forecast also narrows it, so compare with the control.
Coverage: the share of outcomes inside the interval. Neither sign is better; the
target is 80%. CRPS scores the whole predicted distribution.
A variable set is the list of inputs the XGBoost model is given. G0: sun position, ERA5 solar
radiation (ssrd), and air temperature (t2m). Each group adds to the one before.
G1: total cloud cover. G2: low, mid, and high cloud cover. G3: clear-sky radiation.
G4: cloud water and cloud base height. G5: direct beam. G6: wind and thermal radiation.
G7: humidity and haze. G8: snow and albedo. G9 (the full set): all other ERA5 variables.
Negative control: G2 plus shuffled copies of the other variables, which carry no information.
MARS-only: 12 ERA5 variables that neither ECMWF's free forecast feed nor Open-Meteo serves.
Clearness index: irradiance divided by the irradiance at the top of the atmosphere.
Exploratory: not named in the study plan before any result existed, and not corrected for multiple comparisons.
